land.text: the three northern states, the land Cliopatria's Federated Republic of Mexico shape of 1840 gives up to this row

predecessors.note: The federalist north rose against the centralist government; Cliopatria draws Mexico as two rows in these years (federated-republic-of-mexico for the north, centralist-mexico for the core) and the Federated dossier records the loss of these three states in January 1840.

land.text: the three states returned to the Centralist Mexican government after the surrender at Camargo on 6 November 1840

successors.note: Cliopatria's Republic of the Rio Grande row runs to 1841 and the Centralist dossier records the return in 1842; the page dates the surrender to 6 November 1840.

capitals.name: Laredo
capitals.note: The page: the rebels sought a federal republic 'with Laredo as the capital'; the infobox gives Laredo as capital (until March 1840).

capitals.name: Victoria (Texas)
capitals.note: 'President Cardenas and the new government fled to Victoria, Texas'; the infobox dates the move to March 1840. Cárdenas and other officials re-entered Laredo a few days after 6 November 1840 to surrender.

correction.text: the claimed territory of the republic, unchanged, for 1840 only: 'The new state was to include the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas' (rebellion 17 January to 6 November 1840); the Cliopatria year 1841 returns to the Mexican government

keyframe_review.note: Years only: the page has the rebellion end with Canales's surrender at Camargo on 6 November 1840 and is silent on 1841. The 300,402 km2 shape is the three claimed states; the page gives no area, so the ratio cannot be checked, and it names only a few towns the rebels held (Laredo, Guerrero, Mier, Camargo, a raid on Ciudad Victoria) while 'the lack of support from the state governments' means the claim was larger than the control. Render the claim as the rebel hatch; a stricter reading would be the river towns only.

region.text: the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas: 'The new state was to include the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas, with its capital at Laredo'

ledger.note: 1840: northern federalists proclaim the Republic of the Rio Grande near Laredo. 'On January 17, 1840 a meeting was held at the Oreveña Ranch near Laredo' where notables of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas advocated a federal republic 'with Laredo as the capital'; 'Despite the lack of support from the state governments, the Republic of the Rio Grande was formed' and Jesús de Cárdenas was sworn in as president. Confidence 2: the three states are the territory the republic 'was to include', not land the page shows the rebels holding (it names only Laredo, Guerrero, Mier and Camargo) (reviewer am-08-f).

1840: the government retreats to Victoria, Texas. 'President Cardenas and the new government fled to Victoria, Texas' (the infobox gives March 1840); Antonio Canales kept the field as commander-in-chief.

region.text: the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas: 'The new state was to include the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas, with its capital at Laredo'

ledger.note: 1840: Canales surrenders at Camargo and the republic ends. Antonio Canales 'surrendered at Camargo' on 6 November 1840; a few days later 'President Cardenas and other officials entered Laredo to officially surrender'. The page does not describe any Mexican reoccupation or 1841 events. Confidence 2: the three states are the territory the republic 'was to include', not land the page shows the rebels holding (it names only Laredo, Guerrero, Mier and Camargo) (reviewer am-08-f).

region.text: the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas: 'The new state was to include the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas, with its capital at Laredo'

ledger.note: 1840: the Republic of the Rio Grande dissolves; its claimed land is back under the Mexican government. Confidence 2: the three states are the territory the republic 'was to include', not land the page shows the rebels holding (it names only Laredo, Guerrero, Mier and Camargo) (reviewer am-08-f).

wars.name: Rio Grande rebellion

zones.text: the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas: 'The new state was to include the Mexican States of Coahuila, Nuevo León, and Tamaulipas, with its capital at Laredo'

wars.outcome: The federalist rebellion of 17 January to 6 November 1840 failed: Canales fought the Mexican army at Santa Rita de Morelos, San Fernando (where he lost 250 of his 400 men), Mier, Monterrey's outskirts and Saltillo (25 October 1840) and surrendered at Camargo on 6 November 1840.
wars.note: Texas's 'official stance ... was neutral', but Lamar 'secretly encouraged Texans to volunteer' and gave Canales arms. The page dates only Zapata's execution at Guerrero (29 March 1840), Saltillo (25 October) and the surrender; the other battles are undated, so no contest events are recorded for the Mexican government's side.

certainty.note: The republic's extent is a claim to three states, not a held frontier; the page names only river towns the rebels held.

sources.title: Republic of the Rio Grande
sources.note: Identity, 17 January 1840 declaration, the three states, Laredo, Victoria (Texas), battles, the 6 November 1840 surrender.

sources.title: Antonio Canales Rosillo
sources.note: Thin on dates: confirms the republic's 'short existence' in 1840; no territorial detail.

notes: Cliopatria row 1840-1841 (300,402 km2 = Coahuila, Nuevo León, Tamaulipas) is the rebels' claim, not their control; the page ends the republic on 6 November 1840, so 1841 belongs to the Mexican government (Centralist Mexico, which the Centralist dossier shows regaining the land in 1842 from Cliopatria's shapes). Pages used: 2, the second thin. Undated on the page: the Santa Rita de Morelos, San Fernando, Mier and Monterrey fights, the recapture of Laredo, Guerrero, Mier and Camargo, Cárdenas's swearing-in; no contest events recorded. Counterparts: federated-republic-of-mexico (the row that loses the three states in January 1840 in its own dossier) and centralist-mexico (the government that crushed the rising); republic-of-texas (Cliopatria 1836-1845) supplied volunteers but was officially neutral and is not a belligerent here. Gazetteer: no new names; the Laredo capital uses Laredo (Texas) coordinates.
